paper.title: PAC Ranking from Pairwise and Listwise Queries: Lower Bounds and Upper Bounds

settings.name_in_paper: PAC Top-k Item Selection (k-IS) under the MNL model with l-wise queries
unmapped: PAC (epsilon-)top-k: return k items each with score >= theta_[k] - epsilon, with probability >= 1-delta
each query is an l-sized subset of the n items; the winner is drawn from the MNL (Plackett-Luce) choice model
RBC condition: ratios of preference scores bounded by a constant C_rbc
the learner knows l, k and (to set alpha) the RBC constant C_rbc
settings.definition_quote: [PAC Top-$k$ Item Selection ($k$-IS)] Given a set of $n$ items, $k\in\{1,2,3,...,\left\lfloor n/2 \right\rfloor\}$, $l\in\{2,3,4,...,n\}$, $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, we want to find a correct $\epsilon$-top-$k$ subset with error probability no more than $\delta$, and use as few $l$-wise queries as possible.

settings.name_in_paper: Exact top-k item selection under MNL with l-wise queries
unmapped: exact top-k identification from l-wise MNL winner feedback
RBC condition: ratios of preference scores bounded by a constant
settings.definition_quote: Define $\Delta_k:=\theta_{[k]}-\theta_{[k+1]}$. ... to find the exact top-$k$ subset with error probability no more than $\delta$

settings.name_in_paper: PAC Total Ranking (TR) under the MNL model with l-wise queries
unmapped: PAC total ranking: return an epsilon-ranking (full permutation) with probability >= 1-delta
each query is an l-sized subset; winner drawn from MNL model
RBC condition: ratios of preference scores bounded by a constant C_rbc
the learner knows l and (to set alpha) the RBC constant C_rbc
settings.definition_quote: [PAC Total Ranking (TR)] Given a set of $n$ items, $l\in\{2,3,4,...,n\}$, $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, we want to find a correct $\epsilon$-ranking with error probability no more than $\delta$, and use as few $l$-wise queries as possible.

conditions: there exists a hard instance (worst case)
any algorithm finding an epsilon-top-k subset with error probability at most delta

source.label: LB-k-IS
source.quote: Given $\epsilon \in (0, \sqrt{1/32}]$, $\delta \in (0, 1/4)$, $6 \leq k \leq n/2$, and  $2\leq l \leq n$, there is an instance such that to find an $\epsilon$-top-$k$ subset with error probability no more than $\delta$, any algorithm must conduct $\Omega( \frac{n}{\epsilon^2}\log{\frac{k}{\delta}} )$ $l$-wise queries in expectation.

results.notes: n mapped to K. The proof is a reduction from Bernoulli PAC subset selection (Kalyanakrishnan et al. 2012). Algorithm class: delta-correct algorithms.

symbols.Delta_k: theta_[k] - theta_[k+1], the gap between the k-th and (k+1)-th preference scores

conditions: any algorithm finding the exact top-k subset with error probability at most delta

source.label: LB-k-IS2
source.quote: Define $\Delta_k:=\theta_{[k]}-\theta_{[k+1]}$. Given $\Delta_k \in (0, \sqrt{1/32}]$, $\delta \in (0,1/4)$, $6 \leq k \leq n/2$, and  $2\leq l \leq n$, there is an instance such that to find the exact top-$k$ subset with error probability no more than $\delta$, any algorithm must conduct $\Omega( \frac{n}{\Delta_k^2}\log{\frac{k}{\delta}} )$ $l$-wise queries in expectation.

results.notes: Derived from Theorem 1 with epsilon < Delta_k.

conditions: any algorithm finding a correct epsilon-ranking with error probability at most delta

source.label: LB-TR
source.quote: Given $\epsilon \in (0, \sqrt{1/32}]$, $\delta \in (0, 1/4)$, and $2\leq l\leq n$, there is an instance such that to find a correct $\epsilon$-ranking with error probability no more than $\delta$, any algorithm must conduct $\Omega\left( \frac{n}{\epsilon^2}\log{\frac{n}{\delta}} \right)$ $l$-wise queries in expectation.

results.notes: Proved by reduction to top-(n/2) selection.

symbols.alpha_tune: algorithm input alpha balancing error probability and sample complexity

conditions: RBC condition: preference score ratios bounded by constant C_rbc

source.label: TP-TR
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, PDTR terminates after $O(\frac{n}{\alpha^2\epsilon^2}\log\frac{n}{\delta})$ $l$-wise queries, and, if $\alpha \leq \frac{l-1}{4(l+C-1)}$, returns a correct $\epsilon$-ranking.

results.notes: With alpha = Omega(1) the paper states O(n/eps^2 log(n/delta)), which matches Theorem 3.

symbols.C_rbc: RBC constant bounding preference score ratios

conditions: RBC condition: preference score ratios bounded by constant C_rbc

source.label: TP-TopK1
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, PDKS terminates after $O(\frac{n}{\alpha^2\epsilon^2}\log\frac{n}{\delta})$ $l$-wise queries, and, if $\alpha\leq  \frac{l-1}{4(l+C-1)}$, returns a correct $\epsilon$-top-$k$ subset of $A$.

symbols.C_rbc: RBC constant bounding preference score ratios

conditions: RBC condition: preference score ratios bounded by constant C_rbc

source.label: TP-TopK2
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, TNKS terminates after $O(\frac{n}{\alpha^2\epsilon^2}\log\frac{k+l}{\delta})$ $l$-wise queries, and, if $\alpha\leq \frac{l-1}{4(l+C-1)}$, returns a correct $\epsilon$-top-$k$ subset of $A$.

results.notes: With alpha = Omega(1) this is O(n/eps^2 log((k+l)/delta)). That is optimal for l=2 or l = poly(k).
